mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) and a deceleration in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a shift from consumer-oriented to capital-goods investment, which historically precedes cyclical equity drawdowns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO rises and HOUST falls by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which compresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS falls for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a rise in the consumer price index above 3% over two months signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which historically precedes equity market corrections over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > +0.5% MoM for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows by more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average +5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for two consecutive months.
